Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system. It is so big that more than 1,000 Earths could fit inside it. Jupiter is made mostly of gas, so you could not stand on it. Its Great Red Spot is a giant storm that has been swirling for more than 150 years. Can you imagine a storm bigger than Earth?

Honeybees live together in a hive. A single hive can hold thousands of bees, but it has only one queen. Worker bees collect nectar from flowers and turn it into honey. They also carry pollen, which helps plants make seeds and fruit. When a bee finds good flowers, it does a special dance to tell the others where to go!

The water cycle moves water all around our planet. First, the sun warms water in oceans and lakes, and it rises into the air as water vapor. Next, the vapor cools and forms clouds. When the drops in a cloud get heavy, they fall as rain or snow. Then the water flows back to the sea, and the cycle starts again.

Why do leaves change color in the fall? Leaves are green because of chlorophyll, which helps them make food from sunlight. As the days get shorter and cooler, trees stop making chlorophyll. As the green fades, hidden yellow and orange colors start to show, and some trees also make new red colors.

Bread dough rises because of yeast, a tiny living thing that eats sugar in the dough. As it eats, it gives off a gas called carbon dioxide. The gas makes small bubbles that puff up the dough. Bakers often let dough rise for about 1 to 2 hours before they bake it. That's why fresh bread is soft and full of holes!

A volcano is an opening in Earth's crust. Deep underground, it is so hot that some rock melts into a thick liquid called magma. When magma comes out of a volcano, we call it lava. Over time, lava cools and hardens into new rock. Some islands, like the ones that make up Hawaii, were built by volcanoes over many years.

A plant starts as a small seed. When the seed gets water and warmth, it sprouts, and a tiny root grows down into the soil. Then a shoot pushes up toward the light. The plant's leaves use sunlight, water, and air to make food. With good care, a bean seed can sprout in about 1 week.

Our family drove to the beach on a sunny Saturday. We left at 8:00 in the morning and got there by 10:30. Mia built a sandcastle with 3 towers, and Leo dug a moat around it. We found shells, watched the waves, and ate sandwiches under a big umbrella. Before we left, we made sure to pack up all our trash.

The octopus is a clever sea animal. It has 8 arms covered with suction cups that help it grab food and hold onto rocks. An octopus also has 3 hearts and blue blood! Many octopuses can change color to blend in with their surroundings. Because they have no bones, they can squeeze through very small spaces.

Mars is the fourth planet from the sun. People call it the Red Planet because its soil is full of rusty iron dust. Mars has 2 small moons, named Phobos and Deimos. A day on Mars is only about 40 minutes longer than a day on Earth. Scientists send robot rovers to explore its rocky, dusty surface.

The moon is Earth's closest neighbor in space. It does not make its own light; instead, it reflects light from the sun. As the moon travels around Earth, we see different amounts of its sunny side. These changing shapes are called phases. It takes about 29 and a half days for the moon to go through all of its phases.

Your heart is a strong muscle about the size of your fist. It pumps blood through your body all day and all night. Blood carries oxygen and food to every part of you. When you run or jump, your heart beats faster to keep up. You can feel your heartbeat by placing 2 fingers gently on your wrist.

Penguins are birds that cannot fly, but they are amazing swimmers. Their wings work like flippers to help them zoom through the water. Most penguins live in the southern half of the world. Emperor penguins are the tallest kind, and they can grow to about 4 feet tall. A thick layer of fat and tightly packed feathers keeps them warm.

A rainbow forms when sunlight shines through drops of rain. Each drop bends the light and splits it into colors. The colors always appear in the same order: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet. To see a rainbow, stand with the sun behind you and the rain in front of you. Have you ever seen a double rainbow?

A butterfly goes through 4 stages in its life. It begins as a tiny egg, often laid on a leaf. The egg hatches into a hungry caterpillar that eats and grows. Next, the caterpillar forms a chrysalis, where its body changes. Finally, a butterfly comes out, dries its wings, and flies away to find flowers.

The sun is a star, just like the ones we see at night. It looks bigger and brighter because it is much closer to us. Light from the sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. The sun gives us heat and light, and plants use its energy to grow. Never look straight at the sun, because it can hurt your eyes.

Magnets can pull on some metals without even touching them. Every magnet has 2 ends, called the north pole and the south pole. If you put 2 north poles together, they push apart. If you put a north pole near a south pole, they snap together! Try testing objects around your home to see which ones a magnet will pick up.

Snowflakes form high in the clouds when water vapor freezes onto tiny bits of dust. Most snowflakes have 6 sides or 6 points. As a snowflake falls, it can grow bigger and change shape. People like to say that no two snowflakes are exactly alike. On a snowy day, you can catch flakes on a dark mitten and look at them closely.

Elephants are the largest animals that live on land. An elephant's trunk is really a long nose and upper lip joined together. It uses its trunk to breathe, smell, drink, and pick up food. Elephants also flap their big ears to help them stay cool. A baby elephant, called a calf, stays close to its mother for years.

We have seasons because Earth is tilted. As Earth travels around the sun, different parts of it lean toward the sun at different times. When our part of Earth leans toward the sun, we get summer, with long, warm days. When it leans away, we get winter. A full trip around the sun takes about 365 days, which is one year.

Making lemonade is easy and fun. First, squeeze the juice from 4 lemons into a pitcher. Then add 1/2 cup of sugar and 4 cups of cold water. Stir until the sugar disappears, and taste it to see if it needs more. Add some ice, pour a glass, and enjoy it on a hot afternoon!

Every Tuesday at 4:00, Ava and her dad walk to the library. She likes to pick 3 new books each week. Last time, the librarian asked, "Have you tried a mystery?" Ava chose one about a missing cat, and she couldn't put it down. Now she's reading every mystery on the shelf!

The blue whale is the largest animal that has ever lived. It can grow to about 100 feet long, which is longer than 2 school buses parked end to end. Even so, it eats some of the smallest animals in the sea: tiny shrimp-like creatures called krill. A blue whale can eat tons of krill in a single day.

Kids usually have 20 baby teeth. Around age 6, these teeth start to get loose and fall out. Grown-up teeth then grow in to take their place, and most adults end up with 28 to 32. To keep your teeth healthy, brush them twice a day for 2 minutes each time. Don't forget to floss, too!

Ants live and work together in large groups called colonies. Each ant has a job; some gather food, some care for the young, and some dig tunnels. Ants can carry things much heavier than their own bodies. They leave scent trails so other ants can follow the path to food. That's why you often see ants marching in a line!

Saturn is the sixth planet from the sun, and it's famous for its rings. The rings are made of countless pieces of ice and rock. Some pieces are as small as grains of sand, while others are as big as houses. Saturn is mostly gas, and it is so light for its size that it could float in a giant tub of water!

Trees are some of the oldest living things on Earth. When a tree is cut down, you can count the rings inside its trunk to learn its age (each ring stands for 1 year of growth). Trees give us shade, wood, and fruit. Their leaves take in carbon dioxide from the air and give off the oxygen that we breathe.

Frogs start life in the water as tiny eggs. The eggs hatch into tadpoles, which have tails and breathe with gills. Over many weeks, the tadpoles grow back legs, then front legs. Their tails slowly shrink, and their lungs develop. Soon they hop onto land as young frogs, ready to catch bugs with their long, sticky tongues!

Learning to tell time is a useful skill. A clock has 12 numbers, an hour hand, and a minute hand. The short hand points to the hour, and the long hand points to the minutes. When the long hand is on the 6 and the short hand is halfway between 3 and 4, the time is 3:30. What time do you usually eat lunch?

Sound is made when something vibrates, or moves back and forth very quickly. When you pluck a guitar string, it shakes and makes the air around it shake, too. Those vibrations travel to your ears, and your brain hears them as sound. Short, tight strings make high notes, while long, loose strings make low notes. Try humming while you gently touch your throat!

A desert is a place that gets very little rain, usually less than 10 inches in a whole year. Not all deserts are hot; some, like the land around the South Pole, are freezing cold. Desert plants, such as cactuses, store water in their thick stems. Many desert animals rest in the shade during the day and come out at night when it's cooler.

On Saturday morning, Sam and Lily noticed that their neighbor's yard was covered in leaves. They grabbed 2 rakes and got to work. In about an hour, they made 5 big piles. Their neighbor smiled and said, "Thank you so much!" She brought them warm apple cider, and they all sat on the porch together.

Spiders are not insects. Insects have 6 legs, but spiders have 8. Many spiders spin silk to build webs, which they use to catch their food. Spider silk is thin, but it is very strong for its size. Some spiders don't build webs at all; instead, they hunt by jumping or by waiting quietly for bugs to pass by.

Your skeleton holds you up and protects the soft parts inside you. An adult has 206 bones, but a newborn baby has even more. As babies grow, some of their bones join together. The smallest bone in your body is in your ear, and the longest is in your thigh. Eating healthy food and playing outside help keep your bones strong.

Hummingbirds include the smallest bird in the world. They flap their wings so fast that the wings make a humming sound. Hummingbirds can hover in one spot, and they can even fly backward! They drink nectar from flowers using their long beaks and tongues. Because they use so much energy, they need to eat many times a day.

Sloths are slow-moving animals that live in the rain forests of Central and South America. They spend most of their lives hanging upside down in trees. A sloth moves so slowly that tiny green plants called algae can grow in its fur! This green color helps it blend in with the leaves. Most sloths climb down to the ground only about once a week.
